ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r5.claim: The universe's evident signs already attest to God's providence, mercy, wisdom, justice, monotheism, and the Day of Judgement, so no new sign is needed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r5.anchor: why do they not reflect on the ones which are present before them all the time

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r1.claim: Anything raised and arched over something is called a roof; the sky is preserved in several possible senses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r1.anchor: وما رفع وسمك على شيء فهو سقف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r2.claim: Qatada says the sky is protected from decay and change through the long passage of time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r2.anchor: حفظ من البلى والتغير على طول الدهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r3.claim: Other explanations are that the sky is prevented from falling without support, protected from shirk and sin, or protected from devils by shooting stars.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r3.anchor: حفظ من السقوط لإمساكه من غير علاقة ولا عماد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits a prophetic report describing the sky as a raised roof and restrained wave, moving like an arrow and protected from devils; if sound, it directly explains the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r4.anchor: إن السماء سقف مرفوع وموج مكفوف يجري كما يجري السهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r5.claim: The sky’s signs include the sun, moon, stars, their courses and timed rising and setting, all displaying wisdom and power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r5.anchor: ما وضع الله فيها من الأدلة والعبر بالشمس والقمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r6.claim: Most read آياتها in the plural; Mujahid and Humayd read a singular, referring either to the whole created sky as one sign or to a generic collective.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r6.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد عن آيتها بالإفراد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says people notice worldly benefits from the sky—light, navigation, and rain sustaining life—but ignore its clear evidence of a Creator.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r7.anchor: هم يتفطنون لما يرد عليهم من السماء من المنافع الدنياوية

SAMIN-DURR:21:32/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:32/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:32/r1.claim: The clause وهم عن آياتها is a new sentence; treating it as a prospective circumstantial clause is weak.
SAMIN-DURR:21:32/r1.anchor: جملة استئنافية، ويضعف جعلها حالا مقدرة.

SAMIN-DURR:21:32/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:32/r2.speaker: مجاهد وحميد
SAMIN-DURR:21:32/r2.claim: Mujahid and Humayd read آيتها in the singular, taking creation as one sign containing many signs or using singular for the generic.
SAMIN-DURR:21:32/r2.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد " عن آيتها " بلفظ الإفراد. جعل الخلق آية، وهي مشتملة

ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r1.claim: The signs of the sky include its sun, moon, and stars; another reading has عن آيتها, treating the sky itself as the greatest sign of God's power and unity.
ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r1.anchor: معناه وهم عن شمسها وقمرها ونجومها، وقد قرئت عن آيتها، وتأويله أن الآية فيها في نفسها أعظم آية

ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r2.claim: A coordinated set of signs can itself be called an āya, since as a whole it points to God's oneness.
ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r2.anchor: وقد يقال للذي ينتظم علامات كثيرة آية، يراد به أنه بجملته دليل على توحيد الله عز وجل.

ASAD-NOTES:21:31/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:31/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:31/r2.claim: The sky is a well-secured canopy, yet people turn away from its signs.
ASAD-NOTES:21:31/r2.anchor: and [that] We have set up the sky as a canopy well-secured?[41] And yet, they stubbornly turn away

ASAD-NOTES:21:31#n41/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:31#n41/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:31#n41/r1.claim: Asad says the protected-sky phrase seems to have a similar meaning to the first sentence of 13:2.
ASAD-NOTES:21:31#n41/r1.anchor: See note 4 on the first sentence of 13:2, which seems to have a similar meaning.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p112/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p112/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p112/r2.claim: The heaven is a flawless, secure roof whose creation is ancient and which has remained intact, with no fissure or decay.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p112/r2.anchor: No one knows when this roof was made and even after the passage of time, it has not become decrepit or inflicted with any flaw.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p112/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p112/r3.speaker: Some exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p112/r3.claim: Some exegetes understand the heaven’s being ‘secure’ to mean that it is protected from the interference of devils.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r1.claim: The signs are abundant, but they cannot benefit people who have shut their eyes to them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r1.anchor: there is no dearth of them; yet what can they serve such people who have shut their eyes from them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r6.claim: The opponents mock the Prophet’s humanity and status and demand a proof of his messengership; the signs of 21:30–33 answer that demand.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r6.anchor: how can he be God’s messenger when he is a human being; he also has no distinction over them in wealth and status.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p403#3/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p403#3/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p403#3/r8.claim: The verb كلأ means to guard and protect, with كلاءة as its verbal noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p403#3/r8.anchor: السبح: العوم، كلأه: حفظه يكلؤه كلاءة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r1.claim: Qatada explains the sky’s protection as preservation from decay and alteration over the long duration of the world; this does not conflict with its eventual folding and destruction at the Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r1.anchor: من البلى والتغير على طول الدهر كما روي عن قتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r2.claim: Another explanation is that the sky is protected from falling.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : من الوقوع وقال الفراء : من استراق السمع بالرجوم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the protection as shielding the sky from the devils’ eavesdropping, by means of shooting stars.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء : من استراق السمع بالرجوم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r4.claim: Al-Alusi objects that protection from eavesdropping makes mention of a roof seem pointless; the proposed answer is that earthly roofs can be climbed by thieves, unlike the sky.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r4.anchor: أنه يكون ذكر السقف لغوا لا يناسب البلاغة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r5.claim: A further interpretation is that the sky is protected from those beneath it, which in turn indicates complete protection for them from the sky.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : إنه للدلالة على حفظها عمن تحتها

ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that the Prophet looked at the sky and called it a raised roof and restrained wave that runs like an arrow and is protected from devils; if sound, the report is not explicit proof of the verse’s meaning, contrary to Abu Hayyan’s claim.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : أن رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r7.claim: Some say the sky is protected from idolatry and sins, but the author says the same objection applies as to the preceding interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r7.anchor: وقيل : من الشرك والمعاصي ويرد عليه ما أورد

ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r8.claim: The sky’s signs indicate God’s oneness, knowledge, wisdom, power, and will; some are as evident as the sun, while others emerge through investigation.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r8.anchor: الدالة على وحدانيتنا وعلمنا وحكمنا وقدرتنا وإرادتنا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r9.claim: Those turning away are heedless of the signs and do not seriously consider them through the lens of faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r9.anchor: ذاهلون عنها لا يجيلون قداح الكفر فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد وحميد
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r10.claim: Mujahid and Humayd read āyatihā in the singular: each thing in the sky suffices as a sign; on this reading, turning away means denying that it clearly proves a Creator.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p38#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد ( عن آيتها بالإفراد ووجه بأنه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r1.claim: The sky is protected from falling, as supported by 22:65.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r1.anchor: من أن تسقط، دليله قوله تعالى: {ويمسك السماء أن تقع على الأرض إلا بإذنه}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r2.claim: Another explanation is that the sky is guarded from devils by meteors, supported by 15:17.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r2.anchor: وقيل: محفوظا من الشياطين بالشهب، دليله قوله تعالى: {وحفظناها من كل شيطان رجيم}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r3.claim: They are the disbelievers, and the signs are the sun, moon, stars, and other created things in the sky; they turn away without reflection or heed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r3.anchor: وهم} يعني الكفار، {عن آياتها} ما خلق الله فيها من الشمس والقمر والنجوم وغيرها، {معرضون} لا يتفكرون فيها ولا يعتبرون بها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:31-32/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:31-32/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:31-32/r6.claim: The sky is protected by God's power from falling, or by His will from corruption and disruption until the appointed time, or from eavesdropping through shooting stars.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:31-32/r6.anchor: عن الوقوع بقدرته أو الفساد والإخلال إلى الوقت المعلوم بمشيئته

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:31-32/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:31-32/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:31-32/r7.claim: The sky's conditions point to the Creator's existence, oneness, power and wisdom; some are sensed, others investigated in natural philosophy and astronomy, yet people turn away without reflection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:31-32/r7.anchor: عن أحوالها الدالة على وجود الصانع ووحدته وكمال قدرته وتناهي حكمته التي يحس ببعضها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r1.claim: After adducing the heavens and earth as signs of God's greatness, the sūrah detailed familiar earthly features and the region's many mountains, then turns to the sky.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r2.claim: The singular sky is used generically because most people observe only the lowest heaven, and because speaking of one protected roof conveys its preservation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r2.anchor: وأفرادها بإرادة الجنس لأن أكثر الناس لا يشاهدون منها إلا الدنيا ولأن الحفظ للشيء الواحد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r3.claim: The sky is a roof over earth, but unlike familiar roofs it is filled with indispensable benefits, including light sources, guidance signs, and ornaments beyond reckoning.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r3.anchor: وهذه مشحونة بالمنافع فأكثر ما ينزل منها ما لا غنى للناس عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r4.claim: This roof is protected from falling by divine power and from devils by meteors.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r4.anchor: أي عن السقوط بالقدرة وعن الشياطين بالشهب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r5.claim: Most people turn away from the sky's innumerable signs, including large and small stars, winds, and rains, which prove God's power over resurrection and His exclusive divinity and perfection.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r5.anchor: الدالة على قدرتنا على كل ما نريد من البعث

BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r6.claim: They fail to contemplate the ordered management of the sky through risings, settings, and celestial arrangement, which indicates calculations governing benefits.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r6.anchor: لا يتفكرون فيما فيها من التسيير والتدبير بالمطالع والمغارب والترتيب القويم الدال على الحساب الدائر عليه سائر المنافع

DURR-FULL:v5p627/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the sky's protected roof as raised.
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا} قال: مرفوعا

DURR-FULL:v5p627/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the sky's signs as the sun, moon, and stars.
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا} قال: مرفوعا {وهم عن آياتها معرضون} قال: الشمس والقمر والنجوم من آيات السماء

DURR-FULL:v5p627/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r3.claim: A report says Jews asked the Prophet what Friday was; he answered that God created night and day during two of its hours.
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة أن اليهود قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما يوم الجمعة قال: خلق الله في ساعتين منه الليل والنهار

BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r1.claim: The sky is called a roof because it is like a roof over the earth.

BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r2.claim: The sky is protected from falling despite having no pillars, from corruption until the appointed time, or from eavesdropping by devils through shooting stars.
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r2.anchor: من الوقوع مع كونها بغير عمد

BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r3.claim: The gnostic's heart is a protected heaven, guarded from the whispers of human and jinn devils; a Prophetic prayer asks God to fill the heart with remembrance and drive away satanic whispers.
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r3.anchor: أن سماء قلب العارف محفوظة من وساوس شيطان الإنس والجن

BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r4.claim: The author cites Masnavi verses saying God's remembrance burns away demonic whispers and diverts the narcissus eye from the vulture.
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r4.anchor: ذكر حق كن بانك غولانرا بسوز

BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r5.claim: The heavenly signs include sun, moon, stars, and other clear markers of God's existence, oneness, perfect workmanship, power, and wisdom; the heedless do not reflect and remain in error.
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r5.anchor: أدلتها الواضحة التي خلقها الله تعالى فيها وجعلها علامات نيرة على وجوده ووحدته وكمال صنعه وعظيم قدرته وباهر حكمته

BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r6.claim: Turning away from the signs means failing to contemplate them and persisting in unbelief and error.
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r6.anchor: لا يتدبرون فيها فيقفون على ما هم عليه من الكفر والضلال

BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r7.claim: The ten traits of the abdals are purity of heart, generosity, truthful speech, humility, patience, private weeping, advising others, compassion for believers, reflection, and learning from things; one should contemplate creation to find knowledge of God.
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r7.anchor: أخلاق الأبدال عشرة أشياء : سلامة في الصدر

BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r8.claim: David saw a tiny worm in his prayer niche and wondered whether God valued its creation; God made it speak, saying it remembered and thanked Him more than David did.
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r8.anchor: روي أن داود عليه السلام دخل في محرابه فرأى دودة صغيرة فتفكر في خلقها

BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r9.claim: True perception of signs means remembering God in everything, a mark of complete believers; spiritual blindness and turning away characterize ignorant unbelievers.
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r9.anchor: فالمقصود برؤية الآيات بالحق ذكر الله تعالى عند كل شيء وهي من أوصاف المؤمنين الكاملين

BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r10.claim: The author cites Masnavi lines portraying deniers as unable, like asses, to recognize the pearl-like value of divine knowledge.
BURSEVI:v5p362#2/r10.anchor: منكر بحرست وكوهر هاى او كى بود حيوان درو يرايه جو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r1.claim: After earth's creation comes heaven by contrast: the earth passage states its benefits, while heaven's creation shows no evident human benefit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r1.anchor: ناسب بحكم الطباق ذكر خلق السماء عقبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r2.claim: Since heaven's benefit is not apparent, the passage highlights people's refusal to reflect on its signs of profound wisdom rather than explicitly thanking them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r2.anchor: ذكر إعراضهم عن التدبر في آيات خلق السماء الدالة على الحكمة البالغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r3.claim: The sky's preservation embeds a blessing: celestial bodies or their parts do not fall on earth, destroy people, or ruin the land and its usefulness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r3.anchor: حفظ السماء من أن تقع بعض الأجرام الكائنة فيها أو بعض أجزائها على الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r4.claim: A saqf is a roof laid on house walls, not a tent covering; calling the sky a roof is a direct simile, as 13:2 says it has no earthly pillars.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r4.anchor: ولا يقال السقف على غطاء الخباء والخيمة . وأطلق السقف على السماء على طريقة التشبيه البليغ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r5.claim: The clause about turning away is circumstantial; heaven's signs include celestial bodies and motions as well as clouds, lightning, and thunder.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p58/r5.anchor: في موضع الحال . وآيات السماء ما تشتمل عليه السماء من الشمس والقمر والكواكب والشهب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r1.claim: Many tafsirs depend on earlier works, differing chiefly in how briefly or expansively they collect material.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r1.anchor: سابق بحيث لاحظ لمؤلفه إلا الجمع على تفاوت بين اختصار وتطويل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r2.claim: He names al-Kashshaf, Ibn Atiyya’s al-Muharrar al-Wajiz, al-Razi’s Mafatih al-Ghayb, al-Baydawi, and al-Alusi among the leading commentaries.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r2.anchor: وإن أهم التفاسير تفسير الكشاف و المحرر الوجيز لابن عطية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r3.claim: His list also includes commentaries on al-Kashshaf and al-Baydawi, Abu al-Suud, al-Qurtubi, legal tafsirs, al-Tabari, and Durra al-Tanzil, attributed to al-Razi or perhaps al-Raghib.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r3.anchor: وتفسير الشهاب الآلوسي ، وما كتبه الطيبي والقزويني والقطب والتفتزاني على الكشاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r4.claim: The extant tafsir of Muhammad ibn Arfa is al-Ubbi’s student notes, closer to commentary on Ibn Atiyya than a complete tafsir, and it does not cover every verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r4.anchor: والموجود من تفسير الشيخ محمد بن عرفة التونسي من تقييد تلميذه الأبي وهو بكونه تعليقا على تفسير ابن عطية أشبه منه بالتفسير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r5.claim: For brevity, he generally omits attribution to the earlier commentaries he uses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r5.anchor: ولقصد الاختصار أعرض عن العزو إليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r6.claim: He distinguishes insights and scholarly questions he has not found in the tafsirs available to him on that particular verse, without claiming originality.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r6.anchor: وقد ميزت ما يفتح الله لي من فهم في معاني كتابه وما أجلبه من المسائل العلمية ، مما لا يذكره المفسرون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r7.claim: He disclaims being the first to make an observation, since another thinker may have preceded him; he invokes the proverb about poets leaving no patch unstitched.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r7.anchor: ولست أدعي انفرادي به في نفس الأمر ، فكم من كلام تنشئه تجدك قد سبقك إليه متكلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r8.claim: Quranic meanings and aims are varied and far-reaching: rulings, manners, and stories appear in their relevant passages, while one verse may cover several themes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r8.anchor: إن معاني القرآن ومقاصده ذات أفانين كثيرة بعيدة المدى مترامية الأطراف موزعة على آياته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r9.claim: Every verse contains subtleties of rhetoric, a Quranic art not given its own dedicated tafsir book as other subjects were.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r9.anchor: ولكن فنا من فنون القرآن لا تخلو عن دقائقه ونكته آية من آيات القرآن ، وهو فن دقائق البلاغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r10.claim: He undertakes to note rhetorical subtleties he perceives in each verse, according to his understanding and capacity for reflection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r10.anchor: من أجل ذلك التزمت أن لا أغفل التنبيه على ما يلوح لي من هذا الفن العظيم في آية من آي القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r11.claim: The tafsir emphasizes the Quran’s inimitability, Arabic rhetorical subtleties, and patterns of usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r11.anchor: وقد اهتممت في تفسيري هذا ببيان وجوه الإعجاز ونكت البلاغة العربية وأساليب الاستعمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r12.claim: He examines links between successive verses; al-Razi attended to this, and al-Biqa‘i wrote Nizam al-Durar, but their treatments leave many verses insufficiently explained.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r12.anchor: واهتممت أيضا ببيان تناسب اتصال الآي بعضها ببعض ، وهو منزع جليل قد عني به فخر الدين الرازي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r13.claim: An exegete is not obliged to explain the coherence of the order of suras.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r13.anchor: أما البحث عن تناسب مواقع السور بعضها إثر بعض ، فلا أراه حقا على المفسر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r14.claim: He outlines each sura’s aims so readers see the Quran’s harmony and beauty rather than treating its words and clauses as disconnected fragments.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r14.anchor: ولم أغادر سورة إلا بينت ما أحيط به من أغراضها لئلا يكون الناظر في تفسير القرآن مقصورا على بيان مفرداته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r15.claim: He carefully verifies Arabic lexical meanings and vocalization, including details missing from many dictionaries.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r15.anchor: واهتممت بتبيين معاني المفردات في اللغة العربية بضبط وتحقيق مما خلت عن ضبط كثير منه قواميس اللغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r16.claim: He says he worked to uncover Quranic meanings, inimitability, and eloquent usage overlooked by prior tafsirs, hoping readers benefit according to their capacity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r16.anchor: فإني بذلت الجهد في الكشف عن نكت من معاني القرآن وإعجازه خلت عنها التفاسير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r17.claim: He presents the work as concise yet comparable to extensive commentaries, and titles it al-Tahrir wa-l-Tanwir, shortened from its full title.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p7/r17.anchor: وسميته تحرير المعنى السديد ، وتنوير العقل الجديد ، من تفسير الكتاب المجيد . واختصرت هذا الاسم باسم التحرير والتنوير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r7.claim: A saqf is what is above; the sky's protection is general, from devils, projectiles, and other harms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r7.anchor: و «السقف» ما علا، و «الحفظ» هنا عام في الحفظ من الشياطين ومن الرمي وغير ذلك من الآفات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r8.claim: The sky's signs include its stars, rain, thunder, lightning, and thunderbolts, among similar phenomena.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r8.anchor: وآياتها كواكبها وأمطارها، والرعد والبرق والصواعق وغير ذلك مما يشبه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r9.claim: One group reads the word for sign in the singular, intending the generic sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r9.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «وهم عن آيتها» بالإفراد الذي يراد به الجنس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r1.claim: The sky is like a roof over the earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r1.anchor: وجعلنا السماء سقفا أي هي الأرض كالسقف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r2.claim: Abu Salih transmits from Ibn Abbas that the sky is guarded by stars against devils.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما بالنجوم من الشياطين قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the sky is protected from falling, except when God permits it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r3.anchor: والثاني محفوظا من الوقوع إلا باذن الله قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r4.claim: “They” are the Meccan unbelievers, and the sky's signs are its sun, moon, and stars.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى وهم يعني كفار مكة عن آياتها أي شمسها وقمرها ونجومها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد والفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r5.claim: Mujahid reads “its sign” in the singular, taking the sky and all it contains as one sign; al-Farra says both readings are sound.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#2/r5.anchor: قال الفراء وقرا مجاهد عن آيتها فوحده فجعل السماء بما فيها آية وكل صواب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340/r3.claim: The sky is a roof over earth shaped like a dome, as also described in 51:47, 91:5, and 50:6.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340/r3.anchor: أي: على الأرض وهي كالقبة عليها، كما قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir explains building as raising a dome, likens the Prophet's saying that Islam was built on five to five supports, and describes this as familiar tent construction among Arabs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340/r4.anchor: والبناء هو نصب القبة، كما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r1.claim: The sky is high and guarded against being reached.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r1.anchor: أي: عاليا محروسا أن ينال. وقال مجاهد: مرفوعا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the sky as raised.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r2.anchor: أي: عاليا محروسا أن ينال. وقال مجاهد: مرفوعا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits a Prophetic description of the sky as a wave held back from people; Ibn Kathir calls its chain unusual.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال رجل: يا رسول الله، ما هذه السماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r4.claim: People fail to reflect on the sky's vastness and height, its fixed and wandering stars, and the sun's immense daily and nightly course; see 12:105.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r4.anchor: أي: لا يتفكرون فيما خلق الله فيها من الاتساع العظيم، والارتفاع الباهر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r5.speaker: ابن أبي الدنيا
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abi al-Dunya recounts an Israelite worshiper who received no cloud after thirty years; his mother concluded that he often looked skyward and lowered his eyes without reflection, which he admitted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r5.anchor: وقد ذكر ابن أبي الدنيا، رحمه الله، في كتابه

JISHUMI:v7p4813/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r9.claim: محفوظا refers back to the roof, while its signs refers to the sky.
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r9.anchor: وذكر (محفوظا) لأنه يرجع إلى السقف وآياتها ترجع إلى السماء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r5.claim: The sky is protected from falling or quaking by God’s power, or from demons eavesdropping by meteors.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r5.anchor: محفوظا حفظه بالإمساك بقدرته من أن يقع على الأرض ويتزلزل ، أو بالشهب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r6.claim: The signs include celestial lights and their ordered courses, risings, and settings, displaying divine wisdom and power.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r6.anchor: عن ءاياتها } أي عما وضع الله فيها من الأدلة والعبر بالشمس والقمر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r7.claim: A singular reading suffices to signify the class of signs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r7.anchor: اكتفاء بالواحدة في الدلالة على الجنس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r8.claim: People notice worldly benefits from the sky but ignore it as a clear sign of the Creator.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p115/r8.anchor: هم متفطنون لما يرد عليهم من السماء من المنافع الدنيوية

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r3.claim: The protected ceiling may mean the sky is guarded against falling onto the earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r3.anchor: محفوظا من أن تسقط على الأرض

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r4.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the sky is protected from devils.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r6.claim: Another possible sense is protected from idolatry and sins.

MUJAHID:v1p410/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p410/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p410/r1.claim: The protected roof of heaven is raised up.
MUJAHID:v1p410/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا ﴾ يعني مرفوعا

MUJAHID:v1p410/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p410/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p410/r2.claim: The signs of heaven from which people turn away are the sun, moon, and stars.
MUJAHID:v1p410/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وهم عن آياتها معرضون ﴾ قال آياتها الشمس والقمر والنجوم وهي آيات السماء

MUQATIL:21:31-33/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:31-33/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:31-33/r3.claim: The sky is a raised roof, protected from devils so they cannot overhear the angels and tell people what they hear.
MUQATIL:21:31-33/r3.anchor: { وجعلنا السمآء سقفا } يعنى المرفوع { محفوظا } من الشياطين لئلا يسمعوا إلى كلام الملائكة

MUQATIL:21:31-33/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:31-33/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:31-33/r4.claim: The signs include the sun, moon, stars, and other celestial signs; people ignore them instead of reflecting on God's handiwork and affirming His oneness.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#3/r1.claim: The sky is kept in its place from falling, as God says that He holds it from falling to earth except by His leave.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#3/r1.anchor: في موضعه عن السقوط كما قال ويمسك السماء أن تقع على الأرض بإذنه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, the sky is guarded from devils by flaming projectiles, as another verse says.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#3/r2.anchor: أو محفوظا بالهشب عن الشياطين كام قال وحفظناها من كل شيطان رجيم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#3/r4.claim: The signs in the sky include the sun, moon, and stars; the disbelievers turn away without reflecting and believing.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#3/r4.anchor: عن الادلة التي فها كالشمس والقمر والنجوم ﴿ معرضون ﴾ غير متفكرين فيها فيؤمنون

QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r3.claim: One view says the sky is protected from falling on earth, supported by 22:65.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r3.anchor: أي محفوظا من أن يقع ويسقط على الأرض دليله قوله تعالى: ويمسك السماء أن تقع على الأرض إلا بإذنه

QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r4.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the sky is guarded by stars against devils, as in 15:17.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r4.anchor: وقيل: محفوظا بالنجوم من الشياطين قاله الفراء. دليله قوله تعالى: وحفظناها من كل شيطان رجيم

QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r5.claim: Other explanations say the sky is protected from demolition and breach, from being reached by human devices, or needs no supporting pillars.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r5.anchor: وقيل: محفوظا من الهدم والنقض، وعن أن يبلغه أحد بحيلة. وقيل: محفوظا فلا يحتاج إلى عماد.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r7.claim: Another view says the sky is protected from associating partners with God and from sins.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r8.claim: They refers to the unbelievers; Mujahid says the signs at issue are the sun and moon.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r8.anchor: يعني الكفار { عن آياتها معرضون } قال مجاهد! يعني الشمس والقمر.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r9.claim: The signs are attributed to heaven because they are placed there, though elsewhere they are attributed to God as their maker; the unbelievers fail to reflect on its signs and the divine power they show.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r9.anchor: وأضاف الآيات إلى السماء لأنها مجعولة فيها، وقد أضاف الآيات إلى نفسه في مواضع، لأنه الفاعل لها.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r10.claim: Had they considered the sky, night and day, sun, moon, orbits, winds, and clouds, they would know one powerful creator and see that He cannot have a partner.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r10.anchor: بين أن المشركين غفلوا عن النظر في السموات وآياتها، من ليلها ونهارها، وشمسها وقمرها، وأفلاكها

QASHANI:21:30-32/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:21:30-32/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:21:30-32/r6.claim: The sky is the rational faculty, raised above and protected from change, forgetfulness, and error, though people turn away from its arguments and proofs.
QASHANI:21:30-32/r6.anchor: سماء العقل { سقفا } مرتفعا فوقهم { محفوظا } من التغير والسهو والخطأ

RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r1.claim: The sky is called a roof because, in relation to the earth, it is like the roof over a house.
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r1.anchor: سمى السماء سقفا لأنها للأرض كالسقف للبيت

RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r2.claim: One explanation is that the sky is protected from falling, as ordinary roofs may fall; cited verses say God holds it up and sustains the heavens and earth.
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r2.anchor: أن محفوظ من الوقوع والسقوط الذين يجري مثلهما على سائر السقوف

RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r3.claim: A second explanation is that the sky is protected from devils, as stated in 15:17.
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r3.anchor: الثاني : محفوظا من الشياطين قال تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r4.claim: One account says angels protect the sky from devils.
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r4.anchor: أحدهما : أنه محفوظ بالملائكة من الشياطين

RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r5.claim: Another account says stars protect the sky from devils.
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r5.anchor: والثاني : أنه محفوظ بالنجوم من الشياطين

RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r6.claim: Razi prefers protection by angels because it magnifies the gift of divine guardianship; stars are not needed to prevent harm to the sky from jinn stealing a hearing.
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r6.anchor: والقول الأول أقوى لأن حمل الآيات عليه مما يزيد هذه النعمة عظما

RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r7.claim: The sky's signs are the evidences and lessons in its movements, directions, risings and settings, and the precise order of conjunctions and separations, all showing wisdom and power.
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r7.anchor: معناه عما وضع الله تعالى فيها من الأدلة والعبر في حركاتها وكيفية حركاتها وجهات حركاتها

RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r8.claim: A reading has the singular آيتها, understood generically: people notice worldly benefits from the sky but turn away from its manifest evidence for the Creator's existence and oneness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p142#2/r8.anchor: قرىء عن آيتها على التوحيد والمراد الجنس

RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r1.claim: After saying people ignore the sky's signs, Razi details them: sun and moon complete God's favors by producing day and night and benefits through seasonal change and their orbital motions.
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r1.anchor: لما قال : { وهم عن ءاياتها معرضون } فصل تلك الآيات ههنا

STUDYQURAN:21:32/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:32/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:32/r1.claim: “Preserved” can mean guarded from satans, or elevated and protected from falling upon the earth.
STUDYQURAN:21:32/r1.anchor: Preserved means preserved from the satans

STUDYQURAN:21:32/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:32/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:32/r2.claim: The sky as a canopy is also described elsewhere in the Quran.

STUDYQURAN:21:32/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:32/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:32/r3.claim: The idolaters turn away from the heavens' signs, including the sun, moon, and stars.
STUDYQURAN:21:32/r3.anchor: It is said the idolaters turn away in the face of the signs of the heavens, including the sun, moon, and stars

TAB-FULL:v16p263/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p263/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p263/r1.claim: God made the sky a raised roof over the earth and protects it from every rejected devil.
TAB-FULL:v16p263/r1.anchor: وقوله: {محفوظا} [الأنبياء: 32] يقول: حفظناها من كل شيطان رجيم

TAB-FULL:v16p263/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p263/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p263/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses the sky's roof as raised.
TAB-FULL:v16p263/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {سقفا محفوظا} [الأنبياء: 32] قال: مرفوعا

TAB-FULL:v16p263/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p263/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p263/r3.claim: Qatāda describes it as a raised roof and as a contained wave.
TAB-FULL:v16p263/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا} [الأنبياء: 32] الآية: سقفا مرفوعا، وموجا مكفوفا

TAB-FULL:v16p264/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p264/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p264/r1.claim: The polytheists turn from the sky's signs rather than contemplate their evidence for the creator's oneness and exclusive right to worship.
TAB-FULL:v16p264/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: {وهم عن آياتها، معرضون} [الأنبياء: 32] قال: الشمس والقمر والنجوم آيات السماء

TAB-FULL:v16p264/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p264/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p264/r2.claim: Mujāhid identifies the sky's signs as the sun, moon, and stars.
TAB-FULL:v16p264/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: {وهم عن آياتها، معرضون} [الأنبياء: 32] قال: الشمس والقمر والنجوم آيات السماء

TAB-FULL:v1p105/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r1.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r1.claim: The Prophet names the Fatiha Umm al-Quran, Fatiha al-Kitab, and the seven oft-repeated verses.
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r1.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «هي أم القرآن، هي فاتحة الكتاب، وهي السبع المثاني»

TAB-FULL:v1p105/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r2.claim: It is called Fatiha al-Kitab because it opens the written codex and prayer recitation, and precedes the other suras in reading and writing.
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r2.anchor: وسميت فاتحة الكتاب، لأنها يفتتح بكتابتها المصاحف، ويقرأ بها في الصلوات

TAB-FULL:v1p105/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r3.claim: Umm al-Quran means the leading, encompassing source; Arabs call a thing that gathers and leads its related parts an umm, such as the head's covering or an army banner.
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r3.anchor: لتسمية العرب كل جامع أمرا أو مقدما لأمر، إذا كانت له توابع تتبعه، هو لها إمام جامع أما

TAB-FULL:v1p105/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r4.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's banner poem uses umm for the standard that gathers the group under it when they travel or meet an enemy.
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r4.anchor: على رأسه أم لنا نقتدي بها … جماع أمور لا نعاصي لها أمرا

TAB-FULL:v1p105/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r5.speaker: قيل
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r5.claim: Mecca is called Umm al-Qura either because it precedes and gathers the settlements, or because the earth was spread from it as their mother.
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r5.anchor: وقد قيل: إن مكة سميت أم القرى، لتقدمها أمام جميعها، وجمعها ما سواها

TAB-FULL:v1p105/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r6.claim: Humayd ibn Thawr calls fifty the mother of numbers below it because it encompasses them.
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r6.anchor: لأن الخمسين جامعة ما دونها من العدد، فسماها أما

TAB-FULL:v1p105/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r7.claim: All reciters and scholars agree the Fatiha consists of seven verses, but disagree whether the basmala counts and which verse is seventh.
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r7.anchor: فإنها سبع آيات، لا خلاف بين الجميع من القراء والعلماء في ذلك، وإنما اختلفوا في الآي التي صارت بها سبع آيات

TAB-FULL:v1p105/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r8.speaker: أعظم أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r8.claim: The majority of Kufans count the basmala among the seven verses; this view is also reported from Companions and Successors.
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r8.anchor: أعظم أهل الكوفة: صارت سبع آيات

TAB-FULL:v1p105/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r9.speaker: أعظم قراء أهل المدينة ومتفقهيهم
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r9.claim: The majority of Medinan reciters and jurists exclude the basmala and count “those upon whom You bestowed favor” as the seventh verse.
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي سبع آيات، وليس منهن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، ولكن السابعة أنعمت عليهم

TAB-FULL:v1p105/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r10.claim: Tabari says he has already briefly stated his correct view elsewhere and will fully relate the disagreement in a larger legal work, without restating his choice here.
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r10.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وقد بينا الصواب من القول عندنا في ذلك، في كتابنا اللطيف

TAB-FULL:v1p105/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r11.claim: The Fatiha is called the oft-repeated because it is recited in every obligatory and voluntary prayer; Hasan al-Basri interpreted it this way.
TAB-FULL:v1p105/r11.anchor: فلأنها تثنى قراءتها في كل صلاة تطوع ومكتوبة، وكذلك كان الحسن البصري يتأول ذلك

TABATABAI:21:30-33/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r6.claim: The protected sky most likely means protection from devils, as in the statement that God guarded it from every accursed devil.
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r6.anchor: كأن المراد بكون السماء محفوظة حفظها من الشياطين كما قال وحفظناها من كل شيطان رجيم

TABATABAI:21:30-33/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r7.claim: The sky’s signs are its changing celestial events, which point to unified governance resting on one creator.
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r7.anchor: والمراد بآيات السماء الحوادث المختلفة السماوية التي تدل على وحدة التدبير واستناده إلى موجدها الواحد

TABRISI:21:31-32/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:31-32/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:31-32/r4.claim: In the phrase all swim in an orbit, the nominal clause is circumstantial and fī belongs with yasbaḥūn.
TABRISI:21:31-32/r4.anchor: كل في فلك يسبحون جملة اسمية في موضع الحال وفي يتعلق بيسبحون

TABRISI:21:31-32/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:31-32/r16.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:21:31-32/r16.claim: Al-Jubba’i says the raised sky is protected from devils by the shooting stars cast at them.
TABRISI:21:31-32/r16.anchor: محفوظا من الشياطين بالشهب التي ترمي بها كما قال

TABRISI:21:31-32/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:31-32/r17.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:21:31-32/r17.claim: Another view is that God preserves the sky from falling onto the earth.
TABRISI:21:31-32/r17.anchor: وقيل: محفوظا من أن تسقط إلى الأرض كما قال

TABRISI:21:31-32/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:31-32/r18.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:21:31-32/r18.claim: Al-Hasan says it is kept safe from anyone’s attempt to breach it and from decay or collapse over time.
TABRISI:21:31-32/r18.anchor: وقيل: محفوظا من أن يطمع أحد في أن يتعرض لها بنقض أو أن يلحقها بلى أو هدم على طول الدهر عن الحسن

TABRISI:21:31-32/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:31-32/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:31-32/r19.claim: People turn away from reasoning about the sky’s signs of its createdness and dependence on a creator.
TABRISI:21:31-32/r19.anchor: عن الاستدلال بما فيها من دلائل الحدوث والحاجة إلى المحدث

FARRA:v2p201/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p201/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p201/r2.claim: محفوظا may agree masculine with سقف; محفوظة could agree feminine with السماء, like تغشى/يغشى in 3:154.
FARRA:v2p201/r2.anchor: ولو قيل: محفوظا يذهب بالتأنيث إلى السماء وبالتذكير إلى السقف كما قال (أمنة نعاسا تغشى) و (يغشى)

FARRA:v2p201/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p201/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p201/r3.claim: The singular سقفا is used although the skies are plural because they form a roof over the earth like a house roof.
FARRA:v2p201/r3.anchor: وقيل (سقفا) وهي سموات لأنها سقف على الأرض كالسقف على البيت.

FARRA:v2p201/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p201/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p201/r4.claim: The sky is preserved from devils by the stars.

FARRA:v2p201/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p201/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p201/r5.claim: Its signs are its moon, sun, and stars.
FARRA:v2p201/r5.anchor: فآياتها قمرها وشمسها ونجومها. قد قرأ مجاهد

FARRA:v2p201/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p201/r6.speaker: مجاهد
FARRA:v2p201/r6.claim: Mujāhid reads singular آيتها, treating the sky and everything in it as one sign; both readings are valid.
FARRA:v2p201/r6.anchor: قد قرأ مجاهد (وهم عن آيتها معرضون) فوحد (وجعل ) السماء بما فيها آية وكل صواب

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p286/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p286/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p286/r1.claim: The sky is protected from devils by the stars.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p286/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p286/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p286/r2.claim: People turn away from the signs and lessons contained in the sky.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p286/r2.anchor: وهم عن آياتها معرضون} أي عما فيها: من الأدلة والعبر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r1.claim: Saqf means a house's roof; the sky is to the earth as a roof is to a house, and is named the raised roof in 52:5.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r1.anchor: والسماء للأرض كالسقف للبيت، فجعلت السماء سقفا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، الكلبي، الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the sky is guarded from devils by stars; al-Kalbī agrees and al-Farrāʾ chooses this interpretation, supported by 15:17.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: من الشياطين بالنجوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq offers another interpretation: God preserves the sky from falling to earth except by His permission, as 22:65 says.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r3.anchor: وذكر أبو إسحاق وجها آخر قال: حفظه الله من الوقوع على الأرض إلا بإذنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r4.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r4.claim: Another scholar says the sky is preserved from collapse and from the long-term deterioration that affects ordinary roofs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r4.anchor: وزاد غيره: محفوظا من الهدم، ومن أن يلحقها ما يلحق غيرها من السقوف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid glosses the preserved roof as raised.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r6.claim: The author says “raised” conveys the sense rather than a direct gloss: its height preserves the sky because no one can reach it by demolition or artifice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p62#2/r6.anchor: وهذا معنى وليس بتفسير. وذلك أنه مرفوع رفعا لا يطمع أحد أن يناله بنقض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies “they” as the polytheists.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64/r2.speaker: الكلبي وغيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī and other exegetes identify the sky's signs as its sun, moon, and stars.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي وغيره من المفسرين: شمسها وقمرها ونجومها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64/r3.claim: The polytheists turn away by failing to contemplate and reflect on these signs, which would show them that their Creator has no partner.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64/r3.anchor: لا يتدبرونها، ولا يتفكرون فيها، فيعلموا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:31-35/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:31-35/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:31-35/r2.claim: God protected the sky with stars against devils.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:31-35/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:31-35/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:31-35/r3.claim: The sky's signs here are its sun, moon, and stars; people turn away from them without reflecting.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:31-35/r3.anchor: شمسها وقمرها ونجومها { معرضون } لا يتفكرون فيها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r3.claim: The sky is a roof over those below, protected from every rebellious devil, as also stated in 15:17.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r3.anchor: على من تحتها، محفوظا من كل شيطان رجيم كقوله: {وحفظناها من كل شيطان رجيم} [الحجر: 17] .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r4.claim: Here preservation is attributed to the roof, whereas 15:17 attributes preservation to the sky itself.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r4.anchor: وإنما كانت هاهنا محفوظا لأنه قال: {سقفا محفوظا} [الأنبياء: 32] ، فوقع الحفظ فيها على السقف، وفي الآية الأخرى على السماء.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r5.claim: Qatadah describes it as a protected roof and a restrained wave.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r5.anchor: نا سعيد، عن قتادة قال: هي سقف محفوظ، وموج مكفوف

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r6.speaker: ابن مجاهد عن أبيه
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r6.claim: Ibn Mujahid, quoting his father, says the signs are the sun, moon, and stars.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r6.anchor: تفسير ابن مجاهد عن أبيه: يعني الشمس، والقمر، والنجوم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r7.claim: They turn away by failing to reflect on what they see in the sky, which should lead them to recognize the return and believe.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r7.anchor: لا يتفكرون فيما يرون فيها، فيعرفون أن لهم معادا فيؤمنوا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r8.claim: He connects this to 10:101, which commands people to observe the heavens and earth and says signs and warnings do not benefit unbelievers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r8.anchor: قل انظروا ماذا في السموات والأرض وما تغني الآيات والنذر عن قوم لا يؤمنون

ELMALILI:21:30-32/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:30-32/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:30-32/r16.claim: One interpretation is that the sky is protected from the assaults of devils, as 15:17 states.

ELMALILI:21:30-32/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:30-32/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:30-32/r17.claim: Alternatively, the sky is protected from corruption and disintegration until its appointed time, as 35:41 says.
ELMALILI:21:30-32/r17.anchor: vakt-i ma‘lûmuna kadar fesad ve inhilâlden mahfuz

ELMALILI:21:30-32/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:30-32/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:30-32/r18.claim: People turn away from the many signs in the sky that point to God's power and oneness.
ELMALILI:21:30-32/r18.anchor: Semâda Allah’ın kudret ü vahdâniyetine delâlet etmekte bulunan bunca delillerin delâletlerinden yüz çevirip geçiyorlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r1.claim: These verses offer evidence for God’s oneness, uniqueness, and limitless power to recreate the universe and its creatures after they perish.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r1.anchor: Allah’ın birliğini, ortağı ve benzerinin bulunmadığını, bu evren ve içindeki varlıklar yok olduktan sonra onları yeniden yaratabilecek sonsuz güce sahip bulunduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r17.claim: The “protected roof” is understood as both Earth’s atmosphere and cosmic space containing galaxies, solar systems, and stars formed from the nebula’s fragmentation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r17.anchor: 32. âyette geçen “korunmuş tavan” benzetmesinin dünyayı saran atmosferi ve 30. âyette söz konusu edilen nebulanın bölünüp parçalanmasıyla meydana gelen galaksilerin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r18.claim: Cosmic space, created in divine order and balance, moves through centrifugal forces and mutual gravitational attraction, which protect it from collapse.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r18.anchor: Allah’ın kurduğu bir düzen ve denge içinde yaratılmış olan kozmik uzay, merkezkaç kuvvetlere ve karşılıklı kütlesel çekimlere dayanarak hareket etmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r19.claim: The author links this protection to the statement that God preserves the heavens and earth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r19.anchor: bu sistem sayesinde parçalanıp yok olmaktan korunmaktadır (ayrıca bk. Fâtır 35/41)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r20.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r20.claim: Unbelievers ought to learn from the signs of the heavens that show God’s existence and power, yet they turn away.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r20.anchor: Kur’an’da “gökyüzünün âyetleri” diye ifade edilen ve her biri Allah’ın varlığını ve sonsuz kudretini gösteren bu delillerden inkârcıların ibret almaları gerekirken

BURHAN:v3p240/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p240/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p240/r1.claim: Arabic convention commonly places night before day, including in Qur'anic expressions and calendar dating by nights, even though day is masculine and would normally prevail in coordination.

BURHAN:v3p240/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p240/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p240/r4.claim: The sequence putting the heavens and earth before darkness and light, then the sky before night, day, sun and moon, reflects the priority of place over time in creation.

BURHAN:v3p240/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p240/r5.speaker: الطبري
BURHAN:v3p240/r5.claim: Al-Tabari cites reports from Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayra to argue that earth and the sun or light were created before night and day, which are names for periods measured by the sun and moon's motion.
BURHAN:v3p240/r5.anchor: وقد صرح بها الإمام أبو جعفر الطبري في أول تاريخه

NAHHAS:v3p69/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p69/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p69/r1.claim: محفوظا modifies سقف; it could instead be محفوظة modifying السماء.
NAHHAS:v3p69/r1.anchor: نعت لسقف ولو كان محفوظة على أن يكون نعتا للسماء لجاز

ITQAN:v4p535#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p535#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p535#2/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that God made the Preserved Tablet of white pearl with red-ruby pages, luminous pen and writing, and acts each day as He wills.
ITQAN:v4p535#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

BURHAN:v4p131/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p131/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p131/r4.claim: In Arabic, جعل with one object means create; with two it can mean create, name, or transform, so two-object usage alone does not prove creation.
BURHAN:v4p131/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم قاعدة العرب في الجعل إن يتعدى لواحد وتارة يتعدى لاثنين فإن تعدى لواحد لم يكن إلا بمعنى الخلق

ZAJJAJ:v3p389/r14.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p389/r14.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p389/r14.claim: The sky is guarded from falling onto earth except by God's permission.
ZAJJAJ:v3p389/r14.anchor: حفظه الله من الوقوع على الأرض

ZAJJAJ:v3p389/r15.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p389/r15.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p389/r15.claim: An alternative explanation is that the sky is protected by the stars, as stated in the cited passage.

ZAJJAJ:v3p389/r16.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p389/r16.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p389/r16.claim: The closing clause says that they turn away from God's signs.
